title.narrative: Costa Rica Social Risk Management DPL DDO

description.narrative: The Project development objective (PDO) is to strengthen the targeting and efficiency of Costa Rica's social protection system.

The objective of the Social Risk Management Development Policy Loan with a Deferred Drawdown Option Program is to strengthen the targeting and efficiency of Costa Rica's social protection system. It is comprised of two pillars that reflect priorities identified in the 2023 Costa Rica SCD update: improvements of social assistance's targeting and reforms to lessen fragmentation and enhance coordination. The first pillar focuses on improving the poverty targeting of social spending in Costa Rica by strengthening the uptake, robustness, and inclusiveness of its integrated social registry. The second pillar addresses the need to enhance the efficiency of social spending in Costa Rica by reducing fragmentation, improving and coordinating the delivery of social assistance programs, and reducing costs of the delivery of social protection interventions. The stand-alone DPL/DDO modality offers the option of quickly mobilizing liquidity to finance priority spending, including if Costa Rica is hit by climate, social, or economic shocks and needs to cover a targeted and temporary social assistance response. The DPL-DDO supports the government in developing and implementing policies aimed at improving social spending, strengthening adaptation to climate change, and improving opportunities, with a focus on poor and vulnerable groups. The operation also supports outcome area one of the new corporate-score card: protection for the poorest. By improving the targeting and coverage of social assistant programs among the lower income segments of the population the operation directly contributes to advancing these outcome areas. Additionally, by helping improve the adaptiveness of the social protection system, the operation contributes to the prevention and mitigation of the impact of climate shocks among these segments.

title.narrative: RI # 4: Number of women in extreme poor households who are responsible for caring of adults with functional dependency who receive a monthly cash transfer as recognition of their care work.

comment.narrative: There are challenges in identifying eligible populations, particularly severely dependent non-institutionalized individuals (and those in households living in extreme poverty). The target is expected to be achieved after: (i) SINIRUBE adjusts the basic food basket for individuals in households with members with disabilities and functional dependency, considering the additional expenses incurred by the household due to these conditions; (ii) SINIRUBE coordinates with the Costa Rican Social Security Fund and local governments to share information that allows for the identification of a greater number of eligible households.

title.narrative: RI # 4: Number of women in extreme poor households who are responsible for caring of adults with functional dependency who receive a monthly cash transfer as recognition of their care work.

comment.narrative: The progress shown in the indicator is associated with increased application of the BAREMO through home visits; it is expected that these efforts will continue and that the target will be met. As of September 2025, the total number of caregivers receiving the cash transfer stands at 5,606—comprising 4,859 women and 747 men; as agreed, this indicator will report only on progress linked to female caregivers.

title.narrative: RI # 6: Number of beneficiaries who receive their transfer through SUPRES.

comment.narrative: To ensure comparability with the baseline, it is necessary to review the indicator using a cutoff date of December 2025. Furthermore, it is recommended to reinforce—within the SUPRES Steering Committee—the message regarding the need to incorporate other institutions, such as INA, CONAPAM, INAMU, and the Junta de Protección Social, in order to demonstrate progress on the indicator. To achieve the target, it will be necessary to incorporate the Non-Contributory Regime of the Costa Rican Social Security Fund.

title.narrative: RI # 2: Percentage of household surveys in SINIRUBE that was updated in the last 18 months

comment.narrative: The goal is achievable considering that a massive self-application process for the Social Information Form (FIS) will be implemented, which is contemplated as a functionality of the IMAS "my file" application, through which people can enter and update the information collected in the social information form. After that, an IMAS professional would validate that the information entered is consistent and does not distort other information, and will proceed to officially "save" it in the SINIRUBE database.

title.narrative: RI # 5: Percentage of resources from IMAss targeted programs that go to the population of the first income quintile.

comment.narrative: The primary challenge in achieving this goal is the reduction of extreme poverty (the lowest income quintile), which declined from 6.3% in 2023 to 4.8% in 2024. This reduction implies that, despite the allocation of additional resources to this quintile, the percentage of total IMAS resources targeted at households in extreme poverty has not shown significant increases.
